video.title: The Best Low Budget Online Business To Start Right Now

summary: Chris Koerner explains how to sell database reactivation as a service to small businesses using GoHighLevel templates. He proposes a no-brainer, performance-based offer (10% of revenue generated from emailing/texting a client's past-customer list), walks through importing contacts, triggering a workflow, auto-replies, and A/B testing offers. He then suggests upselling other services (AI voice agents, missed-call text back, review automation, chatbots). The video is promotional for GoHighLevel via his affiliate link, and the revenue maths is hypothetical.

speakers.name: Chris Koerner
speakers.description: Host of Koerner Office; says he owns a tree trimming business and uses GoHighLevel daily

ideas.name: Database reactivation agency
ideas.one_liner: Email/text a small business's old customer list with an offer using GoHighLevel templates, taking a share of revenue generated.
ideas.business_model: Performance fee (10% of revenue generated) or flat fee (about $1,000) whichever is less; possible recurring retainer
ideas.customer: Local small businesses with a past-customer list (e.g. tree trimming, roofing)
ideas.problem: Businesses hold lists of past customers but do not market to them, and do not know how to run or A/B test campaigns
ideas.offer: Done-for-you reactivation campaign by email and/or SMS to their past customers, free upfront, paid 10% of revenue generated

pricing.model: Percentage of revenue, or flat fee, whichever is less; could be done free as a foot-in-the-door

price_points.label: flat fee or 10%, whichever is less

pricing.notes: Tracking the client's revenue is hard, hence the flat-fee fallback. Reactivation can be free to get in the door and sell other services.

acquisition_channels.details: Approach local business owners directly with a no-brainer, zero-risk offer (pitch example given for a tree trimming owner); specific outreach method not stated

quote.text: this is what's called a no-brainer offer
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.delivery: Agency owner gets the client's customer list (from QuickBooks, Xero, Stripe, Square, POS), imports a CSV into GoHighLevel, tags contacts to trigger the Recipe List Reactivation workflow, which sends emails/SMS, auto-replies to positive responses with a booking link, follows up, and A/B tests offers. Screenshots of analytics are sent to the client. Client does the actual jobs.
unit_economics_claims: 4,000 emails x 2% = 80 quote requests; half close = 40 jobs x $1,000 = $40,000; 10% = $4,000 (hypothetical)
1,000 roofing customers might yield 1-3 jobs worth $20-50k
ideas.startup_cost: GoHighLevel subscription (price not stated); 30-day free trial via his affiliate link
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: not stated; results within about an hour of sending to see which A/B variant wins

acquisition.how: Finding and pitching local business owners is mostly human. Cold email to limited companies is legal in the UK, but cold SMS/email to sole traders is not, and many local trades are sole traders.

onboarding.how: Needs the client to supply the list and agree on an offer. Import and mapping are tool-driven but need a human to collect and check data.

delivery.how: The workflow, auto-replies, follow-ups, A/B splits and analytics run automatically from a template. Agents could draft offers and copy; a human reviews.

billing.how: Revenue share needs trust and manual verification of the client's jobs; a flat fee is easier to automate with invoicing.

support.how: Reporting by screenshot can be automated. Client questions and reply handling by agents with occasional human checks.

uk_applicability.notes: The model works, but UK PECR/GDPR require consent or a valid soft opt-in for marketing emails/SMS to past customers of individuals and sole traders. The client must own the relationship and supply lawful data, with unsubscribe handling. Tree trimming seasonality and ZIP/US tools differ; GHL is available in the UK.

risks: Emailing/texting old customers without valid consent breaches UK PECR/GDPR
Cannot verify client's revenue under a rev-share deal
Deliverability, spam complaints and stale lists
Clients may find out it is just a template and cut you out

tactics.name: No-brainer performance offer
steps: Ask the owner if they have a customer list and roughly how many emails
Offer to email the whole list with a seasonal special for free
Take 10% of any revenue generated; nothing if zero
Alternative: charge $1,000 or 10%, whichever is less, to guarantee some payment

quote.text: I charge a,000 bucks for this or 10% of any revenue I bring you or whichever is less
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Build the reactivation workflow in GoHighLevel
steps: Automation > Create workflow > From template > search 'reactivation' > Recipe List Reactivation
Import client CSV via Contacts > Import, map fields, apply a tag
Set the tag as the workflow trigger
Edit the email/SMS offer with first-name personalisation
Wait for reply up to 1 hour, check if positive, auto-reply with booking link
Add follow-up steps and publish
Review delivery, bounce, unsubscribe, spam, open, click, reply stats under Marketing > Emails

tactics.name: A/B test offers across the same list
steps: Add a random split (e.g. 50/50) in the workflow
Copy all actions into the second branch
Change the offer (e.g. free quote vs discount vs buy two get third free)
Check per-branch statistics to find the winner within about an hour
Reuse the winning offer for similar businesses in the same niche

quote.text: you can know within an hour of sending this email which one crushes the best
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Ongoing triggers beyond one-off blast
steps: Birthday emails with a 10% coupon
Customer anniversary messages
Stripe payment processed, delay 365 days, then reactivation sequence

tactics.name: Find the client's list
steps: Suggest sources: QuickBooks, Xero, Stripe, Square, POS email capture
Request a spreadsheet export of past customers

tactics.name: Prove value with analytics screenshots
steps: Run the campaign in-house without mentioning GoHighLevel
Send the client screenshots of the stats
Use the success to upsell other services

warnings.warning: Offers proven for one niche may not transfer to regions with different seasonality.

lessons.lesson: Lead with a zero-risk, performance-based offer to remove the buyer's objections and get a foot in the door.

quote.text: The best way to make money is to make money for other people first.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Spend effort on the client's offer to their customers, not just your pitch to the owner; the offer drives results.
A/B testing is a differentiator small business owners rarely do; reuse winning offers across similar clients in the same niche.
Use a free or cheap first campaign to land and expand into higher-value recurring services.
Prebuilt templates let a non-expert deliver a seemingly complex service quickly, so the value is in sales and offers rather than tech.
Choose niches where outcomes are visible (e.g. roofing) so performance fees are verifiable.

quote.text: in some businesses, it's a lot easier to see if that job actually went through
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Keep sequences simple rather than complex.

quote.text: in my experience, it doesn't need to be complex. Simple is better.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

evidence_quality.rationale: Mostly a promotional tutorial with hypothetical revenue maths; the only first-hand data point is his claimed close rate for his tree business. No real client results are given.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Host promotes GoHighLevel with an affiliate link (30 days free) and says he uses it daily.
